title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 619-622 of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). Π~_Q is a profinite extension of Gal(Q̄/Q) by a modular-type profinite group, plausibly the π1 of the modular orbifold M_{1,1} over Q. M is a group of (partial) Galois sections of it. ρ is a torsion element of order 6, plausibly the automorphism group μ6 of the j=0 elliptic curve. L_ρ ≅ Z/6Z is the cyclic group it generates, Z_ρ its centralizer and N_ρ^* its normalizer. Notation: μ = {±1}, and τ' is an involution of 'complex conjugation' type. The kernels via (ε2, ε3) correspond to the cyclotomic character mod 12, i.e. Ker(Π~_Q → Ẑ* → (Z/12Z)*), which matches the orbifold points of orders 4 and 6. M'(-j̄) = Z^!_{ρ0} is a subgroup of the centralizer. M^0(-j̄) = Ker(ε2) on M'(-j̄). M'''(-j̄) = μ_τ' ⋉ M^0(-j̄) maps isomorphically onto Π'''~_Q, so it is a partial section over that open subgroup.

On this page:
(36) records the decompositions M''' ≃ M'''(-j̄)·𝔖^{+1} and N_ρ^* ≃ M'''(-j̄)·L_ρ.
(37) is a summary diagram of inclusions with indices: M^0 ⊂_2 M' ⊂_6 Z_ρ ⊂_2 N_ρ^*; M' ⊂_4 N_ρ^? ⊂_3 N_ρ^*; M^0 ⊂_2 M''' ⊂_4 N_ρ^?. The indices are consistent: M^0(-j̄) has index 24 in N_ρ^*, as stated on the next page.
(38) defines D_ρ := μ_τ'·L_ρ, with μ_τ' ≅ Z/2Z and L_ρ ≅ Z/6Z. This is a dihedral group of order 12, annotated ≃ D_6, embedded in N_ρ^*.
(39) begins 'induit un isomorphisme d'' and then writes D_ρ ⥲ N_ρ^*, ending with '//'. The page is then abandoned and rewritten as p. 622, where the diagram is refined: Z_ρ splits as 2·3 via M'×μ, and the chains μ_τ' ⊂_2 D_τ' ⊂_3 D_ρ and 1 ⊂_2 μ ⊂_3 L_ρ are added. The aim is to list all intermediate finite-index subgroups between M^0(-j̄) and N_ρ^*, study their mutual normality and the quotients. In short, this is the group-theoretic bookkeeping of the 'decomposition group' of the order-6 orbifold point inside the arithmetic fundamental group, and of the Galois sections attached to it.
errors: (39) as written, D_ρ ⥲ N_ρ^*, cannot be literally true: D_ρ is finite of order 12, while N_ρ^* contains the (infinite, profinite) section group M^0(-j̄) with index 24. The sentence 'induit un isomorphisme d'…' is unfinished. Presumably an isomorphism of D_ρ onto a quotient was intended, e.g. N_ρ^* modulo a normal subgroup of index 12. That would need M^0 or M''' to be normal with D_ρ as a complement, which is unclear since M^0 has index 24, not 12. The page is visibly abandoned and redone on p. 622.

(36) N_ρ^* ≃ M'''(-j̄)·L_ρ: by diagram (37), M''' has index 12 in N_ρ^*, but |L_ρ| = 6. So either the product is not a 'transversal' one or M'''(-j̄) here differs from the M''' of (37). This is a possible inconsistency in the indices, which p. 621 also reflects when it calls M''' 'd'indice 4 de N_ρ*'.

ideas.what: Lattice of finite-index subgroups between a Galois-section subgroup M^0(-j̄) and the normalizer N_ρ^* of a torsion element of order 6 in the arithmetic fundamental group (index-24 lattice)
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition/inertia groups of orbifold points of M_{1,1} and the associated Galois sections (packets of sections at elliptic points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Longue Marche, 1981) for the framework; later work on sections and torsion in arithmetic π1 of M_{1,1} (e.g. Nakamura, Hoshi-Mochizuki), unsure of exact attribution
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981) discusses Galois action and torsion in Teichmüller groups in general terms; this specific computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Dihedral group D_ρ = μ_τ'·L_ρ of order 12 generated by the order-6 automorphism and a 'complex conjugation' involution
ideas.modern_name: Real-structure/complex-conjugation extension of the automorphism group μ6 of the j=0 curve (dihedral D_6)

ideas.what: Kernel of the cyclotomic character mod 12 as the open subgroup over which partial sections exist
ideas.modern_name: Field of definition Q(μ12) for the orbifold-point sections of M_{1,1}

missed.claim: An intended structural statement identifying the dihedral group D_ρ with (a quotient of) the normalizer N_ρ^* is left incomplete and is incorrect as written. Grothendieck restarts the computation on the next page.
missed.quote: Notons que l'inclusion D_ρ = μ_τ'·L_ρ ↪ N_ρ^* induit un isomorphisme d' (39) D_ρ ⥲ N_ρ^* //
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only marginally: it is a step in a detailed but routine description of normalizers of torsion in the arithmetic π1 of M_{1,1}, which bears on section-conjecture-type questions for orbifold points. The result is likely recoverable from modern literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft page of bookkeeping (index diagram, a dihedral subgroup) that is abandoned and rewritten on the next page. It does not appear to contain any new idea or result.
transcription_corrections: In (38) the first factor is μ_{τ'} (annotated ≃ Z/2Z), not μ_12 ≃ Z/12Z. L_ρ is annotated ≃ Z/6Z.
Under D_ρ the annotation reads approximately 'ᐁ D_6' (D_ρ ≃ dihedral group D_6); its placement and exact symbol are uncertain.
In (36) the first line is M''' ≃ M'''(-j̄)·𝔖^{+1} (as confirmed by p. 622), not 𝒞^{+1}.
j carries a bar throughout: M^0(-j̄), M'(-j̄), M'''(-j̄).

In (37) the arrows are drawn as inclusions (hooked arrows) M'(-j̄)=Z_ρ^! ↪_6 Z_ρ ↪_2 N_ρ^*, M'(-j̄) ↪_4 N_ρ^? ↪_3 N_ρ^*, M^0 ↪_2 M'(-j̄), M^0 ↪_2 M'''(-j̄) ↪_4 N_ρ^?. On the page this is a single diagram, not three separate rows.
In (37) Z_ρ^! is written with a subscript ρ (Z_ρ^!), not ρ_0 as on p. 621.
(39) ends with '//', and the preceding sentence 'induit un isomorphisme d'' is unfinished.
